newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended down in slow trading on Monday, with stop-loss selling continuing to depress the key September contract sharply, traders said.
The key September 1996 contract ended at an intra-day low of 2,310 yuan ($278) per tonne, down 90 yuan. It opened at a high of 2,440. The settlement price was 2,410, up from last Friday's 2,397.
The settlement prices are weighted average prices of all contracts transacted on the day and the limit-up and limit-down are calculated according to settlement prices.
October fell 22 yuan to 2,320 yuan, with a settlement price of 2,328, down from 2,334.
Combined volume fell sharply to 8,900 tonnes from 126,700.
Today was the last trading day for the September contract, which will begin delivery on Tuesday.
Traders said stop-loss selling by retail investors who did not want to take spot goods pushed the price sharply down.
"The last batch of speculative buyers had to offset their long positions, with most of them suffering heavy losses over the past few weeks," one trader said.
"After delivery of the September contract, the market will be quiet for some time because there is little open interest in the October contract," he added.
The open interest of the October contract is 5,140 lots and one lot is five tonnes.
Traders said the low open interest showed that both institutions and retail investors were little interested in rice in the short term.
